messages:
maria: quick data dump from tonight's bring-up of the 12B candidate. ran sampling + deterministic evals across fp16, int8, and int4; microbenched latency/throughput with cold vs warm KV-cache and batch sizes 1/4/8. putting numbers and a suggested route matrix below — need product guidance on which two variants we should expose by default (fast vs cheap)

jonathan: awesome, thx. short summary first pls?

maria: tl;dr: int8 gives ~1.9x token throughput vs fp16 with negligible quality hit (~-0.6% acceptability in our 2k human A/B). int4 reduces cost further (~2.7x vs fp16) but shows visible failures on long-context reasoning (~-3.5% acceptability) and hallucination tail increase. latency p95 for batch=1: fp16 190ms, int8 115ms, int4 95ms (single A100-like GPU).

leo: do you have per-1M-token cost calc? product wants $ impact for per-month traffic.

maria: yep, rough unit econ (incl infra + amortized model bits):
```
1M tokens served (approx):
- fp16 (12B): $16.80
- int8 (12B): $8.90
- int4 (12B): $6.20
Notes: includes batching baseline qps=100, KV cache hit ~30% across typical session lengths.
```

kate: where did quality numbers come from? eval set + human raters?

maria: 2k production-ish prompts sampled from search/autocomplete/chat mixes. automatic metrics (perplexity + semantic-similarity) aligned but noisy, so we did pairwise blind human A/B on 500 items. automated regression detector flagged 23 cases for int4 where answer integrity dropped (long context).

product-amy: for GTN guidance — are int8 edge cases acceptable for SLAs? what would you recommend as default route for new customers (self-serve)?

jonathan: my take: expose int8 as default 'balanced' offering. Keep fp16 as 'high-fidelity' fallback for routes requiring strict correctness (code generation, legal). Int4 should be experimental; route only if customer opts into 'low-cost aggressive' and we gate with fallback to int8 on regression signals.

maria: suggestion matrix attached (below as config snippet for routing rules we tested):
```yaml
routes:
  - name: fast
    variant: 12b-int8
    p95_target_ms: 150
    qps_per_gpu: 1200
    cost_bucket: balanced
  - name: high-fidelity
    variant: 12b-fp16
    p95_target_ms: 220
    qps_per_gpu: 700
    cost_bucket: premium
  - name: cheap-experimental
    variant: 12b-int4
    p95_target_ms: 120
    qps_per_gpu: 1700
    cost_bucket: cheap
    rollout: opt-in-only
    quality_gate: human-sample-check + automated-regression-trigger
```

leo: do we have a concrete automated trigger for fallback from int4->int8?

maria: prototype rule: if moving window of 1k responses shows >0.7% drop in semantic-similarity z-score or >0.4% increase in hallucination marker -> switch session to int8 and open 10-sample human audit. infra-bot tested failing path switching under load in staging.

infra-bot: rollout-sim completed: simulation of 10k synthetic sessions switching int4->int8 at threshold produced <0.6% added tail latency to cluster; CPU overhead for policy eval <3%.

kate: what about cold-start KV-cache effects? product teams care about first-response latency.

maria: cold-start p50/p95 batch=1:
- fp16: 120ms / 190ms
- int8: 78ms / 115ms
- int4: 70ms / 95ms
But note: quality delta on cold-start is similar to warmed; int4 still shows reasoning regressions on prompts >1024 tokens.

product-amy: proposal for GTN docs: default expose 'fast' (int8) and 'high-fidelity' (fp16) toggles; mention experimental int4 with explicit warnings + opt-in. include cost delta table. that align with recommendations?

jonathan: yes. also add an A/B prompt set to monitor for long-context regressions if customer enables int4.

leo: ops question: quantized model memory/hosts — do we need a separate pool for int4 to avoid eviction thrash?

maria: yes — int4 memory footprint smaller but quant kernels are more memory-bound in our runtime; recommended separate small pool so we can scale independently and avoid noisy neighbor issues. add a warm standby of int8 for quick fallback.

kate: any flagged regression examples we should surface to customers?

maria: added 8 anonymized examples to the internal doc (link) — typical failure: stepwise multi-hop instructions where int4 omitted a constraint or hallucinated a step.

product-amy: good. next actions I want: 1) PR to docs with the route matrix + cost table, 2) a one-paragraph warning for int4 in onboarding UI, 3) ship monitoring alert for the semantic-sim z-score trigger. can someone own each?

jonathan: i'll take (3) — set up alert + dashboard.

leo: i'll take (2) — add a short banner and opt-in checkbox in console.

maria: i'll open the PR for docs (1) today with the numbers and examples. leaving final wording to product.

product-amy: thanks all. sounds like a clean path: default int8, fp16 fallback for high-risk routes, int4 opt-in with gating. update me once the PR + alerts are live. :thumbsup:
